review_notes: I read the whole file and Mathlib's `Submodule.IsCoideal` and `isCoideal_iff` in Mathlib/RingTheory/Coalgebra/Quotient.lean. I looked for repeated nontrivial reasoning. The only real repetition is the "closed-under-joins" pattern: `isCoideal_span_iff`, `IsCoideal.sup` and `IsCoideal.iSup` each turn the coideal conditions into `P ≤ ker …`, prove the bounds with `span_le`, `sup_le` or `iSup_le`, and convert back to pointwise form. The shared helper would be short, so this is a borderline finding that depends on how much the rubric's "thin wrapper" exclusion applies. Other repeated pieces are routine: the `CoalgHom.ext; obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := mkQ_surjective` openers, and the tensor `map_map` factorisations, which differ in each proof. I did not report those. I could not compile anything, so the proposed rewrites are untested.

findings.excerpt: have hker : (⨆ i, I i) ≤ LinearMap.ker (counit (R := R)) :=
findings.problem: `isCoideal_span_iff` (lines 100-113), `IsCoideal.sup` (lines 170-183) and `IsCoideal.iSup` (lines 188-196) each repeat the same scaffolding. They restate both coideal axioms as `P ≤ LinearMap.ker …`, for the counit and for `(TensorProduct.map P.mkQ P.mkQ).comp comul`. They prove each bound with `span_le`, `sup_le` or `iSup_le`, then convert back with `fun x hx => hker hx` or `LinearMap.mem_ker.mp`. The long `ker ((TensorProduct.map … ).comp comul)` statements are written out four more times, and the `hIker/hJker` blocks differ only in which bound lemma closes them.
findings.proposed_change: Add one helper, e.g. `theorem IsCoideal.of_le_ker {P : Submodule R C} (h₁ : P ≤ LinearMap.ker (counit (R := R))) (h₂ : P ≤ LinearMap.ker ((TensorProduct.map P.mkQ P.mkQ).comp (comul (R := R)))) : P.IsCoideal := ⟨fun _ hx => h₁ hx, fun _ hx => h₂ hx⟩`. The proof is immediate from `LinearMap.mem_ker` being definitional. Then: `sup` is `IsCoideal.of_le_ker (sup_le (fun x hx => hI.counit_eq_zero hx) (fun x hx => hJ.counit_eq_zero hx)) (sup_le (fun x hx => hI.map_mkQ_comul_eq_zero_of_le le_sup_left hx) (fun x hx => hJ.map_mkQ_comul_eq_zero_of_le le_sup_right hx))`. `iSup` is `IsCoideal.of_le_ker (iSup_le fun i x hx => (hI i).counit_eq_zero hx) (iSup_le fun i x hx => (hI i).map_mkQ_comul_eq_zero_of_le (le_iSup I i) hx)`. In `isCoideal_span_iff`, the reverse direction becomes `IsCoideal.of_le_ker (span_le.mpr …) (span_le.mpr …)`. Both rewrites keep the existing hypotheses and imports unchanged.
findings.benefit: The three proofs shrink to the two bound arguments that actually differ. The `ker (map mkQ mkQ ∘ comul)` expression is stated once. Any future join-closure result, such as `sSup` or `span`, can reuse the helper. The gain is modest, because the helper itself is short.

evidence.excerpt: map_mkQ_comul_eq_zero : ∀ ⦃x : C⦄, x ∈ I → TensorProduct.map I.mkQ I.mkQ (comul x) = 0
exact fun x hx => (sup_le hIker hJker) hx
